items.title: George "Tex" Stephens Interview, 1996-01-10
items.q: And I was in the middle of it with Okidoki, Earl Woodbury, who at that time was the owner of Club Valley, and Oynes Butch Curry, who was working for the Courier at the time.

ctx.x: This is also from the Pittsburgh Courier. This is about that. It's from November 7, 1953 of the Pittsburgh Courier. And so maybe you could read it. It's just a little article.

The Chicago Press and Radio Men and Public Relations representative from several fronts met on that Wednesday in the home of James Okidoki Smith down on St. Anthony Street. And we elected Johnny Russo, editor of the Courier, Louisiana Dish and President, along with Elgin Hichu of the Louisiana Weekly as vice president. Now, Elgin Hichu was born in Houston, Texas, and he died in Houston, Texas. He died of diabetes. And when he left the Louisiana Weekly, he went back to Houston, Texas. And I understand one of his…
I want you to read something. This is something from the Weekly. I think we talked about this.
